The deal is expected to close later this quarter or early in Dynatrace’s third quarter, subject to regulatory approval and other closing conditions\. Arize focuses on monitoring and evaluating AI models, applications and agents, including detecting hallucinations, measuring output quality and tracing how AI systems behave\. Dynatrace plans to connect those capabilities with its existing visibility into applications, infrastructure, GPU usage and business processes\. That would give teams a way to follow an AI application from testing and evaluation through deployment and ongoing production monitoring\. The acquisition also gives Dynatrace a stronger foothold with AI developers\. Arize has built its presence around AI observability and open source tools, while Dynatrace has traditionally focused on monitoring applications and infrastructure in enterprise environments\. # Dynatrace To Buy Arize For $915 Mln In Cash, Share Dynatrace, Inc\. \(DT\), a software intelligence and observability platform, said on Thursday that it has inked a deal to acquire Arize for $915 million in cash and stock\. Rick McConnell, CEO of Dynatrace, said: \"Acquiring Arize advances our AI observability leadership, accelerates our roadmap, enhances our long-term growth profile, expands our reach with the developer community, and adds an incredible AI-first team to Dynatrace\.\" Under the terms, the company will acquire Arize for $915 million, which consists of around $815 million in cash as well as replacement equity awards for Arize staff members who join Dynatrace\. Dynatrace plans to fund the acquisition through cash on hand and debt\. The transaction is expected to be closed later this quarter or early in Dynatrace's third quarter\. The acquisition is not expected to materially impact Dynatrace's second quarter fiscal 2027 guidance or ongoing share repurchase drive\. Post transaction, Arize's two founders, Jason Lopatecki and Aparna Dhinakaran, will join Dynatrace\. Jason will continue to lead the Arize team\. # Dynatrace acquires observability firm Arize in $915m deal Dynatrace has agreed to acquire observability specialist Arize for $915 million, as the vendor looks to expand its capabilities across the AI development lifecycle\. The deal will bring together Arize’s AI evaluation technology with Dynatrace’s production monitoring capabilities, enabling customers to evaluate, operate, and continuously improve AI applications\. AI observability has become increasingly important as businesses move AI applications into production, connecting model and agent behaviour with application performance, GPU utilization, infrastructure health, and business processes\. Following closure of the acquisition, Dynatrace said customers will gain continuous coverage across the AI lifecycle, spanning experimentation and deployment readiness, through to runtime evaluation and observability\. The combined offering will also provide context of AI behavior and business impact, as well as an enterprise data foundation for AI workloads powered by exabyte-scale analysis and AI lakehouse capabilities\. # Dynatrace Acquires Arize: $915M Bet That AI Evaluation Starts Before Production gettyimages\.com Dynatrace \(NYSE: DT\) has agreed to acquire Arize, the San Francisco-based AI observability startup, in a cash-and-stock transaction valued at $915 million — the largest acquisition in the AI observability category on record\. The deal, announced August 13, 2026, is built on a specific architectural gap that every enterprise deploying AI agents has encountered but few have solved: the tools developers use to evaluate AI behavior before a system ships almost never talk to the tools that operations teams use to monitor it afterward\. The agreement calls for approximately $815 million in cash plus replacement equity awards for Arize employees joining Dynatrace, subject to customary adjustments\. Dynatrace plans to fund the transaction through cash on hand and its existing credit facility\. The deal is expected to close later in the current fiscal quarter or early in Dynatrace's third fiscal quarter, pending standard regulatory review\. ### What Dynatrace Already Had — and What It Didn't Before this deal, Dynatrace was not without AI observability capabilities\.
